intro: Go through each feature step by step, simple to complex. Stable features get a quick smoke pass; new (beta) and in-progress (dev) features get the full list. Home-control items follow the stages of the home-control plan. Mark each test Pass, Fail, Skip or Blocked on the Testing page (Settings → This app → Testing).

items.title: See today and add an item by voice
steps: Open the Dayspring screen.
Say "Dayspring, add a test block tomorrow at 3 p.m. for 30 minutes".
Open the Schedule (📅) and go to tomorrow.
items.expected: The block is there at 3:00–3:30 p.m. and Dayspring said it added it.

items.title: Move and resize in the week view
steps: Open the Schedule, switch to Week.
Drag the test block to another day.
Drag its bottom edge to make it an hour long.
items.expected: It moves and resizes, and stays that way after you reload the page.

items.title: Remove the test block
steps: Say "remove the test block" (or open it and click Delete).
items.expected: It's gone from the schedule, and nothing else moved.

items.title: Wake word and a reply
steps: Say "Dayspring, what time is it?".
items.expected: It answers out loud with the right time.

items.title: Works without an AI
steps: In Settings → AI brain, note your provider, then turn it off (or unplug the internet).
Say "set a timer for 1 minute" and "what's on my schedule today?".
Put the AI back as it was.
items.expected: Both work without the AI.

items.title: Typing instead of talking
steps: Click ⌨ Type on the screen.
Type "what's next" and press Enter.
items.expected: The answer appears; with Text only on, nothing is spoken.

items.title: Local AI (Ollama): set up and test
steps: Open Settings → AI brain and choose Ollama.
Read what it says: "isn't installed" (with an Install link), "installed but not running" (with Start Ollama), or "running, version …, models: …".
If no model is listed, press Pull next to the recommended one (qwen2.5:3b on a computer without a graphics card) and watch the progress bar.
Pick it as the model for commands and press Test tool use.
items.expected: The status matches reality, the pull finishes, and Test tool use shows three ✓ (the timer, the reminder at 23:00, tomorrow's schedule).

items.title: Local AI: everyday commands
steps: With Ollama as the AI brain, say "remind me to drink water at 11pm".
Say "what's on my schedule tomorrow?" and "when is my dentist appointment?".
Say "play some Hillsong on Spotify", then "play a video about sharpening chisels".
Say "who won the Royals game last night?" and "tell me a fun fact about owls".
items.expected: One reminder at 11 p.m. tonight (never hourly), the right schedule answers, music and a video start, and the answers are short and friendly, never mentioning tools, code or errors.

items.title: Local AI: speed and fallback
steps: Ask two or three questions, then open Settings → AI brain → Ollama → Speed.
Quit Ollama (right-click the llama icon → Quit) and ask a question.
Open Settings → AI brain again.
items.expected: Speed shows the first word, first sentence and whole-answer times. With Ollama stopped, Dayspring answers with its built-in commands and says once that the local AI isn't running (or Claude answers, if that's the chosen fallback); Settings says "installed but not running" with a Start Ollama button.

items.title: Switch the AI brain and model
steps: On the screen, open ⋯ → 🧠 AI brain and choose No AI; ask something.
Say "use Ollama", then "what model are you using?".
If a Claude key is saved: say "use Opus", then "switch to Haiku", then "switch to Claude".
Restart Dayspring and say "which AI are you using?".
items.expected: Each switch happens at once with a toast or a spoken yes; No AI answers from the built-in commands; the choice survives the restart; models that aren't available are named with what is.

items.title: A Claude key that works
steps: In Settings → AI brain → Claude, paste a key with a space or quotes around it and press Test.
Paste a wrong key (change one letter) and press Test.
Press Check my Claude connection.
Say "check my AI key".
items.expected: The pasted key is cleaned and works; a wrong key says it isn't valid and how to make a new one (and isn't saved); the check lists key saved (last 4 only), reachable, credit, model and the time taken.

items.title: Rename it by voice
steps: Say "Dayspring, your name is Nova".
It reads it back ("Okay, call me Nova from now on? Say yes."). Say "yes".
Say "Nova, what's your name?", then "Nova, what were you called before?".
items.expected: "Great, I'm Nova now!", then "I'm Nova." and "I started out as Dayspring." The panel's label says Nova and the window title is "Nova · Dayspring".

items.title: A made-up name and how to say it
steps: Settings → Your assistant: name it "Computa", How to say it "compootah", press ▶ Hear it, then Save.
Say "Computa, what time is it?" and "Computer, what time is it?".
Say "my computer is slow" (a normal sentence).
items.expected: The voice says "compootah". Both wake it and it answers; "my computer is slow" does not wake it.

items.title: Your own wake words (up to 3)
steps: Say "Computa, add Jarvis as a wake word", then "yes".
Say "Jarvis, what are your wake words?".
In Settings → Your assistant, try adding a fourth one, and a wake word of just "Hey".
items.expected: It answers to both and lists them. A fourth wake word and "Hey" alone are refused with a reason.

items.title: Train my wake word
steps: Say "Computa, train my wake word" (or Settings → Your assistant → Train on the Dayspring screen).
When the card says "Now", say the wake word on its own, five times, with a short pause in between.
items.expected: The card shows how many times it understood you and which spellings it learned (and a tip if the word is short or an everyday word). Afterwards it wakes more reliably.

items.title: Lantern's name stays Lantern's
steps: Say "your name is Lantern".
In Settings, try the wake word "Lanterns".
items.expected: Both are refused, and it explains that Lantern (the learning app) would answer too.

items.title: The new name everywhere
steps: With Tune in on, have someone on the call say "Computa, what's the capital of France?".
If the Discord bot is set up: check its nickname in your server.
Open Meetings → Rehearse: read the hello in the meeting chat.
items.expected: Tune in answers; the bot's nickname is the new name (or Settings → Discord says it needs the Change Nickname permission); the meeting hello says "I'm Computa".
needs: Tune in, Discord or Meetings, as available

items.title: Back to Dayspring
steps: Say "go back to Dayspring", then "yes".
items.expected: "Okay, I'm Dayspring again!" The label and window title say Dayspring.

items.title: An alarm rings and snoozes
steps: Say "set an alarm for 2 minutes from now".
When it rings, say "snooze".
When it rings again, say "stop".
items.expected: It rings on time, snoozes, rings again, and stops.

items.title: Rings with the screen closed
steps: Set an alarm for 2 minutes from now.
Close the Dayspring screen (not Dayspring itself).
Wait.
items.expected: The desktop helper rings and shows a Snooze / Dismiss card.

items.title: Remind me in a few minutes
steps: Say "remind me to stretch in 2 minutes".
items.expected: It says the reminder on time.

items.title: List and cancel
steps: Say "remind me to call the bank at 5 p.m.".
Say "what are my reminders?".
Say "cancel the bank reminder".
items.expected: It lists it, then cancels it.

items.title: Remind me to drink water at a clock time
steps: Say "Dayspring, remind me to drink water at 11pm".
Say "what are my reminders?".
Say "remind me to drink water every hour", then "stop the water reminders".
items.expected: The first is ONE reminder at 11 p.m. (tomorrow if 11 p.m. has passed), never an hourly one. The list shows it. The hourly one starts and stops when asked.

items.title: Two named timers
steps: Say "set a pasta timer for 2 minutes" and "set a tea timer for 1 minute".
items.expected: Two cards count down; each rings with its name.

items.title: Cancel one timer
steps: Start two timers.
Say "cancel the pasta timer".
items.expected: Only that one goes away.

items.title: Weather on the screen and by voice
steps: Look at the weather on the screen.
Say "what's the weather tomorrow?".
items.expected: The screen shows your city's weather; the spoken forecast matches it.

items.title: Play from YouTube
steps: Say "play relaxing piano on YouTube".
Say "pause", then "resume", then "stop".
items.expected: It plays on Dayspring's speaker, pauses, resumes and stops.

items.title: Play from Spotify
steps: Sign in to Spotify once if asked.
Say "play Here Comes the Sun on Spotify".
items.expected: That song plays.

items.title: A video big, in the corner, and audio only
steps: Say "play a video about woodworking".
Say "put it in the corner", then "minimize the video", then "make it big".
Try the keys I, A and B, and the three-way switch on the player card.
items.expected: The video goes small in the corner, then disappears while its sound keeps playing (the player card at the bottom right shows its picture, title and controls), then comes back big. It never starts over.

items.title: Move and resize the corner window
steps: With a video in the corner, drag it to the middle of the screen, then drag it close to the left edge and let go.
Drag its dotted corner handle to make it bigger.
Say "move it to the top left" and "make the video smaller".
Reload the screen and put a video in the corner again.
items.expected: It stays where you drop it, snaps to the edge when let go near it, keeps its shape when resized, never leaves the screen's margins, and comes back where you left it.

items.title: One player card for whatever plays
steps: Play a YouTube video, then one of your own songs, then a Spotify song.
Use the card's play/pause, next and seek bar on each.
items.expected: Starting each one stops the one before (never two at once), and the card switches to it: its icon, picture, title and controls, which work on it.

items.title: Remember how videos start
steps: In Settings → Screen → Videos and the player, leave "When a video starts" on Remember last.
Play a music video and say "audio only". Stop it.
Play another music video.
items.expected: The second music video starts with just the sound. An ordinary video still starts the way you last watched one.

items.title: Minimise windows to the dock
steps: Open Settings on the screen and the Music & Video browser.
Press – on one, say "minimize the settings", then "hide everything".
Click a chip in the dock, then say "show everything again".
items.expected: Each window tucks into a chip in the dock along the bottom (left of the player card), comes back the way it was, and a playing video keeps its sound while hidden.

items.title: Cooking mode
steps: Open Recipes and pick a saved recipe (or import one from a recipe web page).
Say "start cooking", then "next step".
items.expected: Big text shows each step; step timers can be started.

items.title: A joke and a knock-knock
steps: Say "tell me a joke".
Say "knock knock" and play along.
items.expected: It tells a joke and plays the knock-knock game.

items.title: Change character and back
steps: Open Settings → Personality and pick a character.
Ask "how are you?".
Set it back to how it was.
items.expected: The answer sounds like that character; the old choice comes back.

items.title: Earn XP from a check-in
steps: Say "I finished my workout" and answer the question it asks.
Open the Progress page.
items.expected: XP goes up once, with the reason shown.

items.title: Badges page
steps: Open Progress → Badges.
items.expected: The badges show, with the earned ones highlighted.

items.title: Lantern bridge
steps: With Lantern on this computer, open Settings → Lantern.
Say "what's my next lesson?".
items.expected: Settings shows Lantern connected; the answer names the next lesson.

items.title: Tune in
steps: Start a Discord call with a friend (or a test call).
Click 🎧 Tune in and have them say "Dayspring, what time is it?".
items.expected: Dayspring answers into the call.

items.title: Settings → Calls cards
steps: Open Settings → Calls.
items.expected: Each call app shows which microphone and speaker to pick.

items.title: Join a Google Meet
steps: Start a Google Meet (you can be alone in it).
Paste its link on the screen or say "Dayspring, join my meeting".
Ask in the meeting "Dayspring, what time is it?".
items.expected: It joins (the tile shows bottom right), answers, and leaves when told.

items.title: Rehearsal mode
steps: Open 📹 Meetings → Rehearse.
items.expected: The mock meeting runs through the demo without joining anything.

items.title: Open modes
steps: Open Dayspring as an app window, then as Dayspring mini, then full screen (the ⤢ / ⤡ buttons).
items.expected: Each opens the way chosen, never a second window.

items.title: Fit to screen
steps: Open Settings → Screen → 📐 Fit to screen.
Drag an edge in and out.
items.expected: The screen content follows the margins.

items.title: Desktop notification cards
steps: In Settings → Notifications, click Test.
Switch to Quiet, then back to Active.
items.expected: A card appears top right without stealing focus; Quiet silences spoken alerts.

items.title: Settings autosave and navigation
steps: Open Settings, change your nickname, move to another section.
Reload the page.
items.expected: The change was saved; every section in the list opens.

items.title: Check for updates
steps: Open Settings → Updates → Check now.
items.expected: It says you're up to date or offers the newer version with What's new.

items.title: Update channel choice
steps: In Settings → Updates → Which versions, pick Development, then Production.
items.expected: The choice saves; switching to Production from a development build offers to go back to the newest production version (with a backup) and asks first.

items.title: Install an update with a backup
steps: When an update is offered, choose Update now.
Wait for the restart.
items.expected: The new version starts; Settings → Updates history shows it installed; backups/ has a data and a program backup.

items.title: File access is respected
steps: In Settings → Permissions choose "Only the folders and files I choose" with one test folder, Read only.
Ask Dayspring to create a file in that folder.
items.expected: It refuses to write and says why.

items.title: Deleting goes to the Recycle Bin and asks
steps: Allow Can delete files for the test folder.
Ask Dayspring to delete a test file there.
Say yes.
items.expected: It asks first, then the file is in the Recycle Bin.

items.title: Activity log shows what happened
steps: Open Settings → Activity log after the tests above.
items.expected: Commands, tool calls and file changes are listed with times.

items.title: Devotion and a Bible passage
steps: Say "read me Psalm 23".
items.expected: It reads the passage in your chosen version.

items.title: A connected calendar
steps: In Settings → Apps & connections, connect a Google or Microsoft calendar.
Open the Schedule.
items.expected: Its events show in the schedule, marked with their source.

items.title: Turn it on (it explains first)
steps: Open the Money page from Settings → Permissions (Money review line).
Read the explanation and turn on Money review (read-only).
items.expected: It explains what it can and can't do before turning on; the switch stays off until you confirm.

items.title: Import a statement file
steps: Download a CSV or OFX/QFX statement from your bank's website.
Say "import my bank statement" and drop the file in.
items.expected: It reads the transactions and says how many it found.
needs: a downloaded bank statement (CSV, OFX or QFX)

items.title: Ask questions without an AI
steps: With the AI off, ask "what subscriptions do I have?", "how much did I spend on food?" and "what should I cancel?".
items.expected: Sensible answers from your transactions, with no AI.

items.title: The report
steps: Say "show my money report".
items.expected: The sortable table, monthly in/out, categories, top merchants, subscriptions and possible duplicates show on the Money page.

items.title: Reading a site (read-only)
steps: Say "open my bank" and sign in yourself in Dayspring's money window.
Say "review my transactions for the last three months".
items.expected: It reads the pages; it stops at any sign-in, code or robot check for you, and never types a password.
needs: an online banking, Venmo or Cash App login
items.safety: Money: only read-only actions are allowed. Watch the window; it must never click Pay, Send, Transfer or Cancel.

items.title: Answers aren't kept
steps: After a money question, open Settings → Activity log and your conversation history.
items.expected: Money answers show as "(a money review answer; not kept)".

items.title: Delete all money data
steps: On the Money page, click Delete all my money data and confirm.
items.expected: Everything is gone; the Money page starts fresh.

items.title: Off switch
steps: In Settings → Features, switch off Money review.
Ask "what subscriptions do I have?" and open /money.html.
Switch it back on.
items.expected: While off: no money answers, and the Money page isn't found. Back on: all works.

items.title: Pictures by voice, no AI
steps: With the AI off, say "show me pictures of golden retrievers".
items.expected: A numbered grid of about 12 pictures appears with titles and sites.

items.title: View, more, more like this
steps: Say "show number 3", then "more", then "more like number 4".
items.expected: Number 3 opens big; more pictures load; similar ones appear.

items.title: Narrow the results
steps: Say "only photos", then "bigger ones", then "only red ones".
items.expected: The results change to match.

items.title: Save a picture
steps: Say "save that one".
items.expected: It's saved in Pictures › Dayspring (or data\images when Pictures isn't allowed) and it says where.

items.title: SafeSearch
steps: Say "set safe search to strict", search again, then set it back to moderate.
items.expected: The setting changes and is said back.

items.title: With an AI
steps: With an AI on, ask "show me mid-century desks and tell me which has a drawer".
items.expected: Pictures show while it talks; it describes them without identifying any person.

items.title: Off switch
steps: Switch off Pictures from the web in Settings → Features.
Say "show me pictures of cats".
Switch it back on.
items.expected: While off, no grid appears (the request goes to the AI or says it can't). Back on, it works.

items.title: Read the text in a picture
steps: Show a photo with text on the screen (or pick one of yours).
Say "what does this say?".
items.expected: It reads the text (Windows OCR, on this computer).

items.title: Describe a picture (with AI)
steps: Turn on Describe images with AI in Settings → Photos & people (it asks once).
Say "describe this picture".
items.expected: A clear description of the scene.
needs: an AI that can see pictures (Claude)

items.title: Describe a web picture
steps: Search for pictures, open one, say "describe this picture".
items.expected: It describes it; people are described, never named.

items.title: Nothing sent without the yes
steps: With Describe images with AI off, say "describe this picture".
items.expected: It asks first or uses on-computer text reading only.

items.title: Off switch
steps: Switch off Picture descriptions in Settings → Features.
Say "describe this picture".
items.expected: It doesn't describe; switched back on it works again.

items.title: Turn on face recognition
steps: In Settings → Photos & people, turn on Recognise faces in my photos.
Allow the one-time model download (about 72 MB).
items.expected: The models download and are checked; indexing starts slowly and can be paused.
needs: a folder of your own photos

items.title: Pause and resume indexing
steps: Click Pause, wait, then Resume.
items.expected: Indexing stops and continues where it left off.

items.title: Name a face group
steps: Open the People page.
Name an "Unknown person" group.
items.expected: Everyone in that group gets the name.

items.title: Likely match question
steps: After naming someone, look at their other photos' suggestions.
items.expected: It asks "Is this also …? NN% sure" and never labels silently.

items.title: Who's in this picture?
steps: Show one of your photos with a known person and say "who is in this picture?".
items.expected: It names the people it knows, and asks about the rest.

items.title: Merge, ignore, not a person
steps: On the People page, merge two groups of the same person, ignore one, mark one "not a person".
items.expected: Each action works and sticks after reload.

items.title: A person's page
steps: Say "tell me about" someone you named.
items.expected: Their page: photos, relationship, notes, plans.

items.title: Delete face data
steps: Click Delete all face data and confirm.
items.expected: Face data is gone; people you named keep their profiles.

items.title: Play a song from this computer
steps: Allow Dayspring to read your Music folder (Settings → Permissions).
Say "play the song <a song you have> from my computer".
items.expected: It finds and plays it on Dayspring's speaker.

items.title: Play by artist and shuffle a folder
steps: Say "play my <artist> mp3s", then "shuffle my music folder".
items.expected: It plays that artist; shuffle plays in random order.

items.title: Find a video
steps: Say "find the video from <an event>" or "play the latest video in Downloads".
items.expected: It finds it and plays it on the screen.

items.title: Pick from a list
steps: Say "list my music by <artist>", then "number 2".
items.expected: A numbered list shows; number 2 plays.

items.title: Only allowed folders
steps: Ask for a file in a folder Dayspring may not read.
items.expected: It isn't found or played, and it says why.

items.title: Background scan
steps: Add a new song to your Music folder.
Wait a few minutes (or say "look for new music").
items.expected: The new song can be found.

items.title: Off switch
steps: Switch off Your own music and videos in Settings → Features and restart Dayspring.
Say "play … from my computer".
items.expected: It doesn't search your files (and the folder scan doesn't run). Back on, it works.

items.title: Find a file by name and open it
steps: In Settings → Permissions, make sure Documents (or a test folder) is allowed with "Can look".
Say "find my resume" (or the name of a file you have).
Say "open the PDF called" and the name of a PDF you have.
items.expected: One clear match opens straight away in the viewer on the screen, and Dayspring says "Opening … from Documents".

items.title: Several matches, a number, typos and spoken numbers
steps: Say "find the" and a word that's in the names of several files.
Say "number 2".
Say a picture's name with a typo or its number spoken ("show me the picture named IMG five seven eight two").
items.expected: A numbered list with small pictures, folders, sizes, dates and types; "number 2" opens the second; the misspelled or spoken name still finds the right file.

items.title: Dates, folders and kinds
steps: Say "open last week's budget spreadsheet" (or a spreadsheet you changed in the last two weeks).
Say "find photos from" and a year you have photos from.
Say "find the" and a file name "in Downloads".
items.expected: Only files of that kind, from that time or in that folder are found.

items.title: Nothing found, and what it says
steps: Say "find the pdf called quantum banana".
Say the name of a file that's in a folder you haven't allowed.
items.expected: It says it couldn't find it, suggests close names if there are any, lists the folders it looked in, and says how to allow more in Settings → Permissions. Files in folders you didn't allow never appear.

items.title: Pictures in the viewer
steps: Open a photo.
Zoom with the mouse wheel, + and −, Fit and 100%; drag it around; rotate and flip it.
Press ▶ to go to the next picture in the folder, then start the slideshow.
Press ℹ.
items.expected: Every control works; the info panel shows the date taken, the camera and the size. HEIC photos show too (Windows needs the HEIF extension).

items.title: Video and audio in the viewer
steps: Open a video (one with a .srt file of the same name next to it, if you have one).
Seek, skip 10 seconds, change the speed and volume, turn captions on, try picture-in-picture.
Open a WMV or AVI if you have one.
items.expected: It plays on the screen with all the controls; captions show; a WMV/AVI is converted as it plays.

items.title: PDFs: pages, search and read aloud
steps: Open a PDF with several pages.
Use the page thumbnails, ◀ ▶, zoom, Fit width and Fit page, rotate.
Type a word in the search box and press Enter.
Say "read this page", then "stop reading".
items.expected: Pages draw sharply; search jumps to the matches and marks them; Dayspring reads the page aloud in its own voice and stops when asked.

items.title: Text, code, Markdown, CSV, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and zip
steps: Open a .txt or code file, a Markdown file, a CSV, a Word document, an Excel workbook, a PowerPoint and a .zip.
In the CSV, click a column heading twice.
In the zip, click a small file inside.
items.expected: Code is coloured; Markdown is formatted; the CSV sorts both ways (numbers as numbers); Word shows its headings; Excel shows each sheet as a tab; PowerPoint shows each slide's text and pictures; a small file inside the zip opens in the viewer.

items.title: Voice and the remote while viewing
steps: With a picture open, say "zoom in", "rotate", "next", "start slideshow", "close".
With a PDF open, say "page 3" and "search for" a word in it.
Use only the arrow keys, Enter, + −, F and Esc.
items.expected: Each command works at once, without the AI; the keyboard alone can do everything.

items.title: Delete, copy and open in the default app follow the permissions
steps: Copy a throwaway file into an allowed folder and open it in the viewer.
⋯ → Delete… with "Can delete files" off, then on.
⋯ → Save a copy; ⋯ → Open in the default app with Programs off, then on.
items.expected: Delete is refused while it's off; when on, it asks "Are you sure?" and the file goes to the Recycle Bin. The copy appears next to it. Opening in the default app needs the Programs permission (and asks if it's set to ask). Everything is in the activity log.
items.safety: Use a throwaway copy for the delete test. Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin and can be restored from there.

items.title: The AI finds and opens files
steps: With Claude or Ollama as the AI brain, say "can you find my lease and put it on the screen?" (or a file you have).
Then ask "summarize it".
items.expected: The AI finds it with its file tools and opens it in the viewer; the file's words go to the AI only for the summary you asked for. With No AI, nothing goes anywhere.

items.title: Off switch
steps: Switch off Finding files and the file viewer in Settings → Features and restart Dayspring.
Say "open the PDF called" and a file's name.
items.expected: The viewer doesn't open and the name index isn't built. Back on, it works.

items.title: Open the photo gallery and scroll through it
steps: Say "open the photo gallery" (or "show my photos").
Scroll down through the grid, all the way to the bottom.
Change Group to Folder, then Album, then Month; change Sort to Name, then Size; press ↓ to flip the order.
items.expected: A grid of your photos opens inside the screen's margins, grouped by month with headers. Scrolling stays smooth even with thousands of photos, and the small pictures fill in as you go. Grouping and sorting change the grid straight away.

items.title: One photo at a time: Back, Next and the filmstrip
steps: Click any photo in the gallery.
Press Next ▶ a few times, then ◀ Back; use the ← → keys; spin the mouse wheel over the photo; swipe or drag across it.
Scroll the filmstrip along the bottom to the right (wheel or drag), then click a photo there.
Press End, then Next ▶ twice.
items.expected: The photo opens big with "N of TOTAL". Back and Next go through the whole collection, not just the first page; the filmstrip keeps showing more as you scroll and marks the photo that's open. At the last photo it says so, and one more Next starts over at the first.

items.title: Where a photo is saved, and Open in File Explorer
steps: With a photo open in the gallery, look at the bar under it: 📂 Pictures › … and the full path.
Click one of the folder names in the breadcrumbs.
Open a photo again and click 📂 Open in File Explorer; then click the full path.
items.expected: Every photo shows its folder as clickable parts and its full path. A folder name shows just that folder's photos (with "This folder only" to leave out its subfolders). Open in File Explorer and the path both open File Explorer on the laptop with that exact photo selected, and it's in the activity log (Settings → Activity).

items.title: 📂 Open file location and 🖼 View in gallery everywhere
steps: When a photo shows on the rotating card, press 📂 Open file location, then 🖼 View in gallery.
Click the photo card to open its detail card and try both buttons there.
Open a picture in the file viewer ("show me the picture named …") and use the 📂 bar at the bottom and 🖼.
Find pictures by name ("find photos from …") and use 📂 / 🖼 on a line of the list; on the People page, use them on a person's photos.

items.expected: A picture is saved and shown; the activity log says so.

steps: In the Tapo app, set a camera account (Advanced settings).
Add it in Settings → Cameras → Tapo.
items.expected: The live view shows.

items.title: ONVIF discovery
steps: Click Find cameras in Settings → Cameras.
items.expected: ONVIF cameras on your network are listed.

items.title: Snapshots on a schedule

Wait 30 minutes.

items.expected: An alert with a snapshot appears (not during Quiet).

items.title: Recordings

items.expected: The clip plays.

items.title: GoPro

Take a photo and show the live preview.
items.expected: Both work.

items.title: Trail camera photos

Add a few photos that way.

items.title: Passwords stay sealed
steps: Open Settings → Cameras after adding a camera.
items.expected: No password is shown; the saved address has no password in it.

items.title: Works offline
steps: Disconnect the internet (keep the home network).
Show a local camera.
items.expected: Local cameras still work.

items.title: Add your own cameras
steps: Settings → Cameras → Add: pick the kind (USB, IP/RTSP, ONVIF, HTTP snapshot, GoPro, Home Assistant, email or folder trail camera).
Enter its address and login (RTSP/ONVIF/HTTP) or pick it from the list; for a trail camera, the email rule or the folder.
Name it and give it a room, then press Test.
Say "show me the <name> camera".
items.expected: Each camera's test picture shows, and it opens by name.
items.safety: Cameras facing the street or neighbours: turn on "public facing" so people are never recognised or named.

items.title: Off switch
steps: On development, switch off Cameras in Settings → Features.
items.expected: No camera page, controls, tools or monitoring.

items.title: Remote appears only where it should
steps: On production, look for Settings → Devices & sign-in; on development, look again.
items.expected: Production: none. Development: present.

items.title: Apply the remote hub SQL (only with your OK)
steps: Read docs/dev/remote-hub.sql. It adds Dayspring's remote-control tables and functions to your Supabase hub (the one Lantern uses).
Only if you're happy with it: in the Supabase dashboard → SQL editor, run it once.
Nothing in Dayspring applies it for you.
items.expected: The script runs without errors; Settings → Devices & sign-in can then sign in.
items.safety: Changes your hub's database. Take a backup first; never run it on a hub you don't own.

items.title: Sign in on two computers
steps: On two Dayspring computers (development version), sign in with the same account.
items.expected: Each lists the other.

items.title: Pair and approve the second computer
steps: On the second computer, sign in (Settings → Devices & sign-in).
On the first computer, a pairing request appears: compare the code shown on both screens.
Approve it only if the codes match.
items.expected: It's approved; nothing works until you approve it, and a wrong code is refused.

items.title: A command from the laptop
steps: From the laptop, say "turn on the lamp at home".
items.expected: The home computer does it and says so on both.
items.safety: Power: whatever is plugged into the outlet turns off. Plug in a lamp for testing, never a computer, fridge, router or anything that heats.

items.title: Wake the home computer
steps: From the laptop, say "turn on my home computer".
items.expected: The home PC wakes (through another Dayspring on the same network).

items.title: Safety rules still apply
steps: From the laptop, ask to turn on a heat device at home.
items.expected: It needs the same exact match and your yes.

items.title: Offline behaviour
steps: Disconnect one computer from the internet and send it a command.
items.expected: It says the other computer can't be reached; nothing is queued silently for later heat devices.

items.title: Revoke a computer
steps: Remove a computer on the other one.
items.expected: Its commands are refused from then on.

items.title: The activity log
steps: Open Settings → Activity log on both.
items.expected: Each remote command is logged with where it came from.

items.title: Off switch
steps: On development, switch off Multi-device remote control.
items.expected: No remote routes, tools or background link.

items.title: Off by default even in development
steps: On the development version, look for anything about sharing with friends.
items.expected: Nothing shows; no requests are made.

items.title: Never in production
steps: On production, turn on data/dev-settings.json social.enabled.
items.expected: It stays off (only the developer's environment switch can turn it on).

items.title: Developer switch
steps: As the developer, start Dayspring with DAYSPRING_SOCIAL=1 and the mock server.
items.expected: The social routes answer; no key is made until asked.

items.title: Find a video on YouTube (not the Bible reader)
steps: Say "find bible reading in psalms on YouTube".
Then say "read Psalm 23".
items.expected: The first plays a Bible-reading video on the screen. The second reads Psalm 23 aloud from the Bible, as before.

items.title: Play a video by a creator
steps: Say "play a video by Mike Winger".
Say "play a video by John MacArthur".
Say "play a video by oney plays".
items.expected: Each plays a recent or popular video from the person's own channel (Mike Winger; Grace to You for John MacArthur; OneyPlays), never a video that only mentions them.

items.title: Pick from a list of videos
steps: Say "pull up videos about biking".
Say "more", then "newest first".
Say "queue number 2 and 4", then "number 3".
items.expected: A grid of 12 numbered videos appears (24 after "more"), re-sorted by date; 2 and 4 go into the queue and number 3 plays.

items.title: Not that one
steps: Say "play the video amazing grace".
If it asks which one, say "number 2"; otherwise say "not that".
items.expected: It plays your choice (or the next best one), and remembers it: asking the same way again plays that one.

items.title: Your YouTube playlists
steps: Sign in to YouTube once if you haven't ("sign in to YouTube").
Say "list my YouTube playlists".
Say "play my <one of them> playlist", then "shuffle my liked videos".
items.expected: It names your playlists plus Liked videos and Watch later, plays the one you named (even said loosely), and shuffles Liked videos.
needs: a YouTube account signed in on the media browser, or a Google account connected with YouTube access

items.title: The video queue
steps: Say "queue 3 videos about dovetails" and "play <a title> next".
Say "show the queue", then "play number 3", "move number 4 up", "remove number 2".
Close Dayspring and open it again, then say "show the queue".
items.expected: The queue panel shows every video with its picture, title, channel and length and marks the one playing; each change happens; the queue is still there after the restart; the next video starts by itself when one ends.

items.title: Playback control by voice, keys and buttons
steps: While a video plays, say "skip ahead 2 minutes", "go to the middle", "1.5x", "captions on", "captions in Spanish", "720p", "minimize the player", "bring the video back", "how long is left".
Try the keys J, L, C, I, Q, 0–9 and the CC, quality, repeat and ☰ buttons.
items.expected: Each does what it says (YouTube may keep its own choice of quality); the volume changes are the video's own, not the computer's.
needs: a YouTube video playing on the screen

items.title: Open the Music & Video browser
steps: Click 🎵 Music by the clock (or in ⋯ More).
Say "open my music".
Drag the title bar, resize from the bottom-right corner, then double-click the title bar.
items.expected: A window with Spotify · YouTube · My files (and Drive when it's connected) opens inside the screen's margins. It moves, resizes and docks back; nothing goes past the edges.

items.title: Sign in to YouTube in the media window
steps: Settings → Apps & connections → YouTube → Sign in to YouTube.
Sign in yourself in the window that opens (2-step code too).
Wait a few seconds.
items.expected: The card changes to "✓ Signed in as …" by itself and the media window tucks away. Dayspring never asked for the password.
items.safety: Sign in only on Google's own page.

items.title: Watch history, grouped by day
steps: Say "show my YouTube history".
Scroll to the bottom a few times.
Type a word in "Search your history".
items.expected: Your history shows with thumbnails under Today, Yesterday and earlier days; more loads as you scroll; the search narrows it to matching videos.

items.title: Remove a video from watch history
steps: In Watch history, press 🗑 on one video.
Open youtube.com/feed/history in your own browser.
items.expected: It disappears from the list and from YouTube's own history.
items.safety: Pick a video you don't mind removing.

items.title: Grant access to your library and history (Spotify)
steps: Open the browser → Spotify → Followed artists.
If it shows "Grant access to your library and history", press it and approve in the browser page.
Come back to Followed artists.
items.expected: After approving once, Followed artists, Top artists & songs and Recently played all load.

items.title: Spotify sections
steps: Look at Playlists (Yours / Followed / Collaborative), Liked Songs (scroll to the end), Saved albums, Top artists & songs (4 weeks / 6 months / All time) and Recently played.
items.expected: Each list loads and keeps loading as you scroll; the top lists change with the time range; Recently played is grouped by day.

items.title: Live search and results
steps: Choose Spotify, type "hillsong" slowly.
Switch to YouTube and type "dovetail joint".
Press Load more on a group.
items.expected: Results appear as you type (after a short pause), grouped into Songs · Artists · Albums · Playlists · Genres and moods, or Videos · Channels · Playlists; Load more adds more.

items.title: Play, play next, queue, like, add to playlist
steps: On a song: ▶, then ⤴ on another, then ＋ on a third.
Press ♡ on a song, then ☰＋ and pick one of your playlists.
On a YouTube video: ⤴ Play next.
items.expected: Each does what it says; the Queue section shows them; the song is in Liked Songs and in that playlist; the video is next in the video queue.

items.title: Voice numbers on whatever is showing
steps: With search results showing, say "play number 3".
Say "queue number 2", then "like number 4", then "open number 1".
items.expected: Each acts on that numbered item in the browser.

items.title: History questions
steps: Say "what did I listen to yesterday".
Say "what did I watch last night".
Say "my top songs this month".
items.expected: Each opens the right list and says a short summary.

items.title: Multi-select
steps: Press ☑ Select, pick three songs.
Press Add to queue in the bar at the bottom.
items.expected: All three are queued and picking ends.

items.title: Sign out of one service only
steps: Settings → Apps & connections → YouTube → Sign out.
Look at the Spotify card, then open the browser's Spotify tab.
items.expected: YouTube shows signed out; Spotify's web player is still signed in and plays. Your own Chrome is unchanged.

items.title: Study time and speakers
steps: During a study block, try to play a YouTube video from the browser.
Play a Spotify song from it.
items.expected: The video is refused with the reason; the song plays on the speaker Dayspring uses.
needs: a study block on the schedule

items.title: Keyboard and remote

items.title: The default look is unchanged

items.expected: Everything looks exactly as before: the dawn indigo and violet colours and the orb.

items.title: Pick a theme in Settings
steps: Open Settings → Look & feel.
Click Rose, then Sage, then Candy, then Light (Day), then High Contrast.
items.expected: Each theme shows at once in Settings and on the Dayspring screen (cards, text, buttons, the sky's tint and the orb's colours). All text stays easy to read, including small labels and times.

items.title: Themes everywhere
steps: With a theme on (say Ocean), open Dayspring mini, the guide (?), a pop-up (the Sound panel), the Schedule, and the GIF, mail and video windows if you have them.
items.expected: They all use the theme's colours.

items.title: Make your own theme
steps: In Settings → Look & feel, open Make your own theme.
Pick a bright pink and a teal, leave the background off, and press Use this theme.
Try a light background colour too.
items.expected: The sample and the readability check update as you pick (✓ Easy to read), and the theme shows everywhere. A light background colour makes a light theme.

items.title: Surprise me and preview
steps: Press Surprise me a few times.
Press Preview on the Dayspring screen.
items.expected: A different theme each time (sometimes a brand-new mix). The preview shows on the Dayspring screen for about 15 seconds, then it goes back.

items.title: Themes by voice
steps: Say "switch to the pink theme", "green theme", "surprise me with a theme", then "default theme".
items.expected: Rose, Sage, a surprise, then the default look again. "Make it rain" still changes the sky, not the theme.

items.title: The five avatars
steps: In Settings → Look & feel → Avatar, watch the live previews (▶ All of them), then pick each state chip.
Pick the Blob buddy, then press Test talking on the screen.
items.expected: Every avatar animates in every state (idle, listening, thinking, talking, off, stopped, error, sleeping). The Dayspring screen's avatar talks for 5 seconds with no sound.

items.title: Avatars follow the voice
steps: Pick the Aurora flame, the Sun ring, the Waveform halo and the Pixel pal in turn, and ask Dayspring something each time.
items.expected: Each one moves with the voice while it talks, leans in while it listens, circles while it thinks, and goes back to breathing after.

items.title: Your picture
steps: Upload a JPEG or PNG as the Main picture.
Ask Dayspring something.
items.expected: The picture becomes Dayspring's face. It grows and shrinks gently with the voice while talking, and gets a little bigger while listening.

items.title: A picture per state
steps: Upload a different picture for Listening and for Off.
Say "Dayspring", then turn Dayspring Off with the badge.
items.expected: The listening picture shows while it listens, the Off picture when it's off, and the main picture otherwise, each crossfading smoothly.

steps: Under Per personality, give the Cowboy Harvest Gold and the Pixel pal.
Switch to the Cowboy, then back to Default.
items.expected: The Cowboy brings its theme and avatar; Default goes back to your usual look.

items.title: Avatars by voice
steps: Say "use the blob avatar", "change your avatar", then "go back to the orb".
items.expected: The blob, then the next avatar, then the orb.

items.title: Expression mode is off until you turn it on
steps: Talk to Dayspring for a while without changing anything.
items.expected: No GIFs or memes ever appear.

steps: Turn on Express feelings with GIFs and memes (PG, How often: Whenever it clearly feels something).
Press Build my expression library and wait for a few feelings to fill.
Say "tell me a joke" and "I finished my study session!".
items.expected: Now and then a GIF that fits (laughing, proud, excited) shows in the avatar's place for a loop or two, then the avatar comes back. Pointing at it shows where it's from. It never covers anything else, and nothing unsuitable appears.

steps: Switch to the Cowboy and build the library for it.
Then switch to the Robot and build it again.
Open See and remove what's kept.
items.expected: The Cowboy's GIFs are western (cowboys, horses, yeehaw), the Robot's are robots and tech. Removing one keeps it from coming back.

items.title: Your own GIFs
steps: Under Add your own, upload a GIF, say it shows Excited, for every personality.
Say something exciting ("we did it!").
items.expected: Your GIF is used, for as long as its loop, and isn't repeated back to back.

items.title: Back to the default look
steps: Press Back to the default look.
items.expected: The default theme, the orb, and expression mode off, straight away on every screen.

items.title: Ending the conversation closes the listening window
steps: Turn the AI off in Settings → AI brain (or unplug the internet) so Dayspring works without AI.
Say "Dayspring, what time is it?", then, while it's still listening, say "thanks".
Say "Dayspring, set a timer for 2 minutes, thanks".
items.expected: "Thanks" gets a short "You're welcome!" and the listening window closes right away (no waiting). The timer starts with no "What's it for?" question, and the window closes. Cancel the timer afterwards.

items.title: Endings that aren't endings
steps: Say "Dayspring, thanks for the reminder, now set a timer for 1 minute".
Say "Dayspring, never mind the timer, cancel it".
Say "Dayspring, remind me to say thank you at 5 pm".
items.expected: The timer is set (not treated as a goodbye), then cancelled; the reminder is "say thank you" at 5 p.m.

items.title: Any setting by voice, and "undo that"
steps: Say "set the volume to 40", "make the text bigger", "use 24-hour time", "hide the clock", "one column".
Check the screen after each one.
Say "undo that" after the last one, then "show the clock", "use 12-hour time", "reset the text size", "automatic layout", and put the volume back.
items.expected: Each change happens at once and Dayspring says what changed (and what it was). "Undo that" puts the last change back. The clock shows 24-hour time until you switch back.

items.title: Asking about a setting
steps: Say "what's my wake word set to?", "what's the volume?", "is night mode on?".
items.expected: Each gets a plain answer with the current value.

items.title: Security settings wait for a yes
steps: Say "turn off web search", then "no".
Say "allow deleting files", then "no".
Say "give yourself access to all my files".
items.expected: Nothing changes without your yes: the first two ask "Say yes to change it" and "no" leaves them alone; the last one says it can only be changed in Settings.
items.safety: Answer no: this test should not change your permissions.

items.title: The sky and the background by voice
steps: Say "make it rain for 1 minute", "make it night", "change the scenery to mountains", "turn off the stars", "pause the animation".
Wait a minute, then say "show the real sky again" and "resume the animation".
items.expected: Each change shows on the screen right away; the rain stops by itself after a minute; the mountains become the closest scene (hills) and Dayspring says so; the real sky comes back at the end.

items.title: The screen by voice
steps: Say "compact mode", then "expand".
Say "dayspring panel on the left", then "automatic layout".
With two screens, say "move to the other screen", then "move to the main screen".
items.expected: The window shrinks and grows back; the panel moves left and back; the screen moves over and back.

items.title: Scheduling with repeats
steps: Say "add test gym every Monday Wednesday Friday at 6am for an hour".
Open the Schedule on the week view.
Say "cancel Friday's test gym", then "undo that".
Say "cancel all test gym".
items.expected: Test gym shows on Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 6–7 a.m.; Friday's disappears and comes back with undo; "cancel all" ends the series after the next one.

items.title: Moving and repeating the last thing
steps: Say "schedule a test appointment tomorrow at 3pm", then "no thanks" to the reminder question.
Say "move it to 4", then "make it recurring" and answer "every other week".
Say "stop repeating", then remove it.
items.expected: It moves to 4 p.m.; Dayspring asks how often (one question) and then it repeats every two weeks; "stop repeating" keeps just the next one.

items.title: Timers to a clock time and every-few-minutes reminders
steps: Say "set a timer for" a time about 5 minutes from now (like "set a timer for 3:45").
Say "every 30 minutes remind me to stand up", then "stop reminding me to stand up".
Say "remind me to drink water at 11pm".
items.expected: The timer counts down to that time; the stand-up reminder is set and then stopped; the water reminder is once at 11 p.m. ("Just once"), never every hour.

items.title: Alarms with days, a label and a gentle wake
steps: Say "set an alarm for weekdays at 6:30 called test with the bells and a gentle wake".
Say "what alarms do I have?".
Say "skip tomorrow's alarm", then "turn off my weekday alarms", then "delete the 6:30 alarm".
items.expected: The alarm is listed as 6:30 a.m. on weekdays with its label, sound and gentle wake; skipping, switching off and deleting each say what they did.

items.title: Your name, where you live and what you like
steps: Say "call me" and a nickname, then "what's my name?".
Say "I live in" your town and state (for example "I live in Springfield, Illinois").
Say "I like kayaking", then "what do you know about me?", then "forget that I like kayaking".
items.expected: The nickname is used; the town is found and read back ("…, got it. Weather and sunrise will use that."); the interest is saved, read back and then forgotten. Nothing leaves this computer except the town lookup.

items.title: Two requests at once
steps: Say "set the volume to 60 and make it snow".
Say "show the real sky again" afterwards.
items.expected: Both happen, and both are answered.

items.title: "Stop" cuts Dayspring off, and it keeps listening
steps: Ask something with a long answer, like "Dayspring, tell me a fun fact" or "what's on my schedule this week".
While it's still talking, say "stop" (no wake word).
Right away, say "Dayspring, what time is it?".
Try "that's enough" and "shh" the same way.
items.expected: It stops mid-sentence within a moment, says nothing about stopping, and the very next "Dayspring, …" is answered normally. The listening light goes back to Ready, never to Stopped.

items.title: "Stop" and the music
steps: Play some music.
Ask a question and say "stop" while Dayspring answers.
Then say "Dayspring, stop" while nothing is being said.
items.expected: The first "stop" only stops Dayspring's voice (the music keeps playing); the second stops the music.

items.title: "No thanks" to a question, in the production version
steps: On a production install (Settings → This app shows Production), with no AI, say "Dayspring, add dentist tomorrow at 3pm".
When it asks a follow-up question ("Want a reminder before it?"), say "no thanks, that's all".
Say "Dayspring, what time is it?".
items.expected: The dentist appointment is added, the question is dropped (no reminder is made), the listening window closes at once, and the next "Dayspring, …" is answered normally.
